Thanks James — good to speak earlier. Quick recap and agreed follow-ups from today:

- Goal: confirm encryption posture we need to meet Paywise security checklist (PII handling, retention, logging, and key management).
- Ask you to confirm: target retention window (regulatory vs business) and whether you require EU-only residency for keys/data.

Key items we'll follow up on: 
1) In-transit: TLS and mTLS options (we support TLS 1.2+/1.3 and mutual TLS for private deployments).
2) At-rest: AES-256 envelope encryption.
3) Customer-managed keys: support for AWS KMS (CMEK), Azure Key Vault, GCP CMEK, and an on-prem HSM connector for Private deployments.
4) Audit/logging: detailed access logs and key-use events; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and retention is configurable (default 90d).

Attachments: redwood-kms-architecture.pdf (brief) attached — should answer most architecture-level questions. I'll follow up with the SOC2 report and a short matrix mapping your checklist items to our controls.

- You will confirm retention target and whether keys must remain in EU.
- If helpful, we can set up a technical workshop with our infra/SRE folks.

Thanks Marissa, helpful recap. A few clarifications from our security team so we can map to our procurement checklist: 

1) Customer-managed keys: we need to know whether Redwood supports true BYOK where Paywise holds key material and Redwood never has the ability to export plaintext or wrap/unwrap outside of envelope flow.
2) HSM options: do you support CloudHSM (AWS) / KeyVault HSM? Any third-party HSM vendors supported? For on-prem HSMs we typically require FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or HSM appliance from Thales/Entrust.
3) Key lifecycle: rotation frequency, automated rotation support, and whether key deletion is irrevocable (we need to understand backup/archival behavior).
4) Audit logs: we require key-use logs retained for up to 7 years and integration with our SIEM (Splunk). Can logs be pushed to our cloud storage bucket or consumed via syslog?
5) Data residency: if we put data in US region, do keys have to be in EU to satisfy our EU customer contracts? Can we pin keys to a region?

Also, please send SOC2 evidence and any KMS architecture docs. If you can provide short bullets for each of the questions above we'll loop in our infra/crypto lead and follow up with a procurement timeline.

Thanks,
James Li
Security Lead, Paywise

Hi James — thanks, below are concise answers to the items your security team raised. Happy to expand any of these in the technical workshop.

1) BYOK / exportability
- Redwood supports envelope encryption with a per-customer Customer Master Key (CMK). For hosted customers we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP CMEK) so the CMK is managed by the customer and never exported to Redwood. Envelope data keys are generated per workload and are wrapped by the customer CMK.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, we offer an HSM connector pattern where the HSM (customer-managed or cloud HSM) performs wrap/unwrap and private key material never leaves the HSM. We do NOT require access to unwrapped key material.

2) HSM support and FIPS
- Supported: AWS CloudHSM, AWS KMS (HSM-backed), Azure Key Vault (HSM), Google Cloud KMS (HSM-backed).
- For on-prem HSMs we support integration with Thales and Entrust via KMIP-compatible connectors in Private deployments; we can validate FIPS 140-2 Level 3 devices where required.

3) Key lifecycle
- Rotation: automatic rotation supported via customer KMS policies; envelope keys are rotated per session/interval.
- Deletion: key deletion is irreversible from Redwood’s perspective; if you delete a CMK in your KMS and we lose access to the wrap/unwrap operation, data encrypted under that key will be unrecoverable. We document the impact and recommend backup/retention policies in the migration guide.

4) Audit logs
- We emit key-use events (wrap/unwrap), admin key configuration changes, and access logs. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (Splunk) via secure syslog or pushed to a customer-controlled storage bucket (S3/GCS/Azure Blob).
- Default retention: 90 days. Contractual extensions up to 7 years are available via add-on (we will include this in the contract SOW).

5) Data & key residency
- You can pin keys to a region by provisioning the CMK in the desired KMS region (AWS/Azure/GCP). For EU-only residency we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated capacity in EU region with CMKs provisioned in the EU.

Attachments and evidence
- SOC2 report: https://drive.redwood/reports/SOC2-2026-Redwood.pdf
- Architecture diagram: redwood-kms-architecture.pdf (attached).

Next steps

- James: if you can share the specific checklist items (or a short matrix) we'll map them directly to the artifacts.
